subject: Term amendment & reserved GPU pool upgrade — proposal and SLA exception request
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Term amendment & reserved GPU pool upgrade — proposal and SLA exception request

Jordan —

Thanks for the time on Thursday. Per our discussion, ACME is looking to increase reserved capacity ahead of your Q4 launch window. I attached a first-pass SOW and a capacity table that maps the GPU mix to throughput projections. High-level summary:

- Current: 8 x A100 (reserved)
- Proposed: add 12 x A100 (reserved) to reach 20 total
- Goal: support sustained peak throughput of ~6k tokens/sec across batch-constrained workloads with 99.9% availability

Two items we need alignment on for contract amendment:
1) Term: ACME requested 18 months (instead of renewing at 12) — this unlocks a committed discount tier.
2) SLA exception: because this is a materially larger pool and involves model warm-up + prefix caching changes, you're asking for a narrower latency p95 commitment for the steady-state SLA. Our standard Dedicated SLA is p95 < 120ms for specific reference models; you asked if we can include a steeper latency SLO and corresponding uptime credits.

To move fast, I've proposed an amendment that:
- Adds the 12 GPUs (detailed in attached CSV)
- Extends term to 18 months and applies a 10% committed spend discount starting month 1
- Includes a 90-day ramp window where latency targets are adjusted: p95 target relaxed to 250ms for the first 90 days, with a phased improvement schedule to 130ms by day 90; uptime credit schedule tied to measurable milestones. If ACME needs an earlier steady-state SLA we can add a performance milestone with partial credits tied to measured p95 on a sample prompt set.

Please review the attached SOW and let me know if procurement/legal want different wording on the SLA exception. If acceptable, I'll route an updated SOW to DocuSign and loop in Legal for an amendment.

Attachments: ACME_SOW_v3.pdf, proposed_capacity_table.csv

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

---

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-ai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Kaitlin Park <kaitlin.park@acme-ai.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term amendment & reserved GPU pool upgrade — proposal and SLA exception request

Rishi —

Thanks, appreciate the clear proposal. A few quick clarifications from procurement/engineering at our side:

1) Throughput: 6k tokens/sec sounds in line with our perf estimates, but can you confirm those numbers assume continuous batching and the Q3 model weights (v2026.06)? We need a short performance appendix.
2) SLA exception: ACME prefers a stricter p95 (<=120ms) starting day 1 if possible. We understand warm-up risk, but our product launch is inflexible. If Redwood cannot meet day-1 p95, we’d accept the ramp but would like additional uptime credits for the first 60 days (not 90) and a clause to pause payments for any sustained >40% deficit in throughput for more than 12 hours.
3) Pricing: the 10% discount is good; can you include a capped add-on price for additional GPUs beyond the 12 in case we expand further?

Procurement timeline: we want to sign by end of July. Can you get updated SOW + performance appendix and a DocuSign link to review?

—Jordan
Jordan Lee
Director, Cloud Engineering — ACME AI
jordan.lee@acme-ai.com

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term amendment & reserved GPU pool upgrade — proposal and SLA exception request

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick feedback. Short answers:
1) Throughput assumptions: yes — numbers assume v2026.06 weights, continuous batching with a 1s batching window, and kernel-level optimizations for attention. I’ve asked Neha to attach a brief performance appendix with raw p95/p50 traces and per-GPU throughput. See latency-dashboard-snapshot.png attached.
2) SLA exception cadence: We can compromise. Proposal below (I’ve updated the SOW):
   - Day 0–30: p95 target relaxed to 220ms; uptime credits = standard SLA * 1.5 for breaches
   - Day 31–60: p95 target <= 160ms; uptime credits = standard SLA * 1.25 for breaches
   - Day 61–90: p95 target <= 130ms; after day 90, standard p95 <= 120ms applies
   - If we miss steady-state p95 (>180ms) for a continuous 12-hour window after day 90, ACME is eligible for a one-time partial reimbursement (pro-rated credits covering impacted hours).
   - For your requested 60-day timeline we can compress the ramp but will require a 15% additional committed spend (or a one-time performance buffer fee) to reserve burst capacity during ramp.
3) Pricing cap for future GPUs: agreed — we’ll include a capped unit price for future A100 reservations within the amendment (valid for the term).

Marissa/Neha/Dylan — can you sanity-check the technical ramp plan and the credit calculations? I want to make sure the metrics and the measurement windows are clearly defined before we send DocuSign.

I’ll prepare an updated SOW that reflects the compressed ramp option and the DocuSign link once we get a thumbs up internally.

Thanks,
Rishi

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term amendment & reserved GPU pool upgrade — proposal and SLA exception request

Jordan, Rishi —

I reviewed the perf traces and the proposed ramp. A few operational points from CS/Onboarding:

- Measurement: we'll define a canonical prompt set (10K tokens worth of mixed short/long) and a synthetic steady-state runner that ACME will run for 48 hours before go-live to validate p95. We'll capture traces in the Redwood Console and export the timeline.
- Warm-up matters: caching and KV warm starts can add tail latency for the first 24–72 hours; the proposed 30/60/90 windows are reasonable if ACME accepts the compressed-ramp fee.
- Fallback policy: recommend including an automatic fallback route to a higher-replica hosted variant for critical endpoints during any sustained breach > 2 hours to protect customer-facing traffic. That fallback will not count against uptime credits but will mitigate outages.
- Credits math: I'll attach a sample calculation table in the SOW (example rows: hours missed, credit %, pro-rated fee).

If ACME agrees to the compressed-ramp fee (one-time fee or higher commit), we can tighten the Day 0 p95 goal from 220ms to 180ms.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: latency-dashboard-snapshot.png

---

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-ai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kaitlin Park <kaitlin.park@acme-ai.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme-ai.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term amendment & reserved GPU pool upgrade — proposal and SLA exception request

Marissa/Rishi —

Thanks — the fallback policy is critical for our launch. We are open to the compressed-ramp fee instead of the 15% higher commit; procurement prefers a one-time performance buffer (capex-style) over increasing the ongoing committed spend. Can you add a one-time buffer fee line to the SOW and specify the amount? We propose $40k as a starting point; happy to review your recommendation.

Also confirm: the canonical prompt set and the 48-hour steady-state runner will be run in ACME's staging project with Redwood telemetry enabled. After run-completion, if p95 <= target for the stage, the Day 0 credit relaxation is voided.

Procurement target: get this signed and in DocuSign by 31 Jul.

—Jordan

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Legal <legal@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term amendment & reserved GPU pool upgrade — proposal and SLA exception request

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick responses and practical approach. Action items:

1) Neha will attach the performance appendix and a recommended one-time buffer fee (ballpark $45k; Neha to confirm exact calc).
2) Marissa will add the credits table and fallback route language into the SOW.
3) I’ll prepare the DocuSign package with the 18-month term amendment, the capped unit price for future GPUs, and the compressed-ramp fee line (one-time buffer).
4) Legal: please review the SLA exception wording below (copied into the SOW draft):
   - Temporary p95 adjustment schedule (Day 0–30: 220ms; Day 31–60: 160ms; Day 61–90: 130ms; Day 91+: standard p95 120ms) OR a compressed ramp to 90 days in exchange for one-time buffer fee.
   - Measurement: canonical prompt set + Redwood Console telemetry; 48-hour verification run required to remove Day 0 relaxation.
   - Credits: pro-rated hourly credits for sustained steady-state p95 > 180ms after day 90; higher credit multiples during the ramp window as previously described.

Jordan, I’ll send the DocuSign link by end of day after Neha confirms the buffer fee and we incorporate Marissa’s credits table.

Thanks all —
Rishi

Attachments (referred): ACME_SOW_v3.pdf, proposed_capacity_table.csv, latency-dashboard-snapshot.png
